Question: Is CA really tough?
Old_Answer: I qualified CA after failing 2 years straight! Let me tell you my story! I come from a very good academic background, from ranking 3rd in my District in 10th grade SLC 11 years back, to almost scoring a rank in CA-Intermediate level back in 2013, I’ve been quite a studious student. Everything was going smooth, not like a cake walk but not a path of thorns either. But then, CA-Final Happened! I joined a CA- Internship which would not allow me to join any classes (back then online classes were not as popular as they are now) and whenever, I joined any class, I’d get out-stationed which would make me miss around 75% of the total class. Normal working hours would be around 16–17 during peak time (4–5 months straight). There are instances where I’d leave home at 6AM, attend my lectures, report to office at 10:30 and then back to home at around 2AM. And with all the unhealthy food from “starred” hotels, and no exercise plus some other unhealthy habits and choices, I got serious health problems, both physical and mental. I was burnt out. (Class in New Delhi: Circa. Feb 2017) I skipped my November,2016 & May 2017 examinations (ICAI conducts exams semi-annually in May and November) as I was quite unprepared and had a baggage of obesity, fatty liver, depression, High cholesterol level, fatigue, palpitation, severe back pain to name a few. (Nepal, Circa. June 2017) I moved to Varanasi, and had a realization that I had enough of these issues. I started taking care of my body. I followed a workout regimen and started studying Indian scriptures mostly Ayurveda and Philosophy along with studying CA Books. (Varanasi: Our Nepali Mandir on top, it has very good vibrations if you want to meditate and bottom two are pictures of our Dharmashaalaa) Then came November, 2017 attempt. I was prepared for my exams, but for some strange reason, in my first paper of Financial Reporting, I reached my Center 30 minutes late (because of unexpected traffic and a goof up) and afterwards, I got blank for 20 minutes. Later, I realized, it was due to antibiotics, which I consumed a month before for my skin problems. I managed to pass all the papers except that one and because of that, I had to take Group-I again (There are 2 groups of papers, 4 each.) Failed because of ICAI’s System Okay, come May, 2018 paper. This time I was sure I’d pass. And, here I failed again because of “Auditing” paper. The irony, I worked at an Audit firm for 3 years. I asked for revaluation and found out that the examiner, for some strange reasons, decided to give 1 out of 4 marks for every question attempted, even if my answers were 100% matching with ICAI’s suggested answers. Because of ICAI’s strange rules, we cannot challenge the examiner. I was very sad and was very angry as well, but this time, I was working out, had my diet in check and had reversed almost all my health problems. I was into meditation and acquired a lot of knowledge in Indian Ayurvedic Systems, Philosophy and spirituality. There were a lot of doubts and a lot was happening in family as well, but that was totally understandable. I was hurt, for sure, but I was pretty confident. I decided to take this one last attempt and finally passed in November, 2018. So, Is CA Really Tough? No. It just requires a lot of discipline not only in studies but also in life overall. Take care of your physical , mental and spiritual health. Follow a workout regimen. If you’re interested I’ve made a beginner workout program: FREE 30 Day Home Workout For Beginners To Lose Weight Or if you’re interested in Yoga: Get Your 30 Days Beginner's Yoga Program Make sure to meditate and keep the positivity and the discipline in track. You can check out my bio to connect with (If you use Pinterest or Instagram), if you’d like help in your journey. What about revaluations? Yes, that is a sad part, and we are working a lot. We even protested back in September, 2019 against it. I, along with other teachers will make sure there is an amendment so that no one would have to go through the pain, that I , and thousands of other students went through. (September, 2019: Protest against ICAI as a Member) How is your journey going by? Let me know in the comments below. Wishing you good health and a good life.

Answer_with_user_profile: Intermittent fasting (IF) has gained popularity as an effective weight management strategy, but concerns regarding its potential impact on kidney health deserve consideration. Extended periods of fasting can lead to dehydration if fluid intake is not adequately maintained during eating windows. Dehydration is a significant risk factor for kidney stones, as concentrated urine can facilitate the crystallization of minerals, leading to stone formation. Moreover, fasting may affect dietary choices during feeding periods, potentially resulting in higher intake of oxalate-rich foods (such as spinach, nuts, and chocolate), which can also contribute to the risk of kidney stones, particularly calcium oxalate stones. Additionally, certain individuals may inadvertently consume less calcium while focusing on restricted eating patterns, which paradoxically can increase stone risk since adequate calcium intake is crucial for binding oxalate and reducing absorption. However, the relationship between intermittent fasting and kidney stone formation can vary significantly among individuals, depending on factors such as hydration levels, nutritional choices during eating windows, pre-existing health conditions, and genetic predisposition. To mitigate risks while practicing intermittent fasting, individuals should prioritize proper hydration and maintain a balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and adequate calcium. It’s advisable for anyone considering long-term intermittent fasting, especially those with a history of kidney stones or related concerns, to consult with a healthcare provider or a registered dietitian to develop a personalized plan that minimizes the risk of adverse effects on kidney health.
Answer_with_full_information: Intermittent fasting (IF) has gained popularity for its potential benefits on weight loss and metabolic health, but its impact on kidney stone formation is a valid concern. Kidney stones primarily form when there’s an imbalance in the substances that make up urine. During intermittent fasting, an individual often experiences changes in fluid intake and dietary patterns, which can influence the concentration of these substances. For instance, prolonged fasting without adequate fluid intake may lead to dehydration, a significant risk factor for stone development. Additionally, if one consumes a diet high in oxalates—found in certain nuts, spinach, and chocolate—while in a restricted eating window, this might exacerbate the risk. However, it's essential to note that research specifically linking intermittent fasting to kidney stones is still limited. Some studies suggest that intermittent fasting can potentially be beneficial for overall kidney health by promoting autophagy, a process that helps in cellular repair and detoxification. The key lies in hydration; drinking sufficient water during eating windows can help dilute urine and prevent stone formation. If you're considering intermittent fasting and are concerned about kidney stones, it’s wise to monitor your hydration levels and dietary choices closely. Consulting with a healthcare professional can provide personalized advice tailored to your health needs. In conclusion, while there isn’t strong evidence to suggest that intermittent fasting directly increases the risk of kidney stones, the potential risks associated with dehydration and dietary imbalances should not be overlooked.

The key is to be patient and flexible; change may not come overnight, but small, consistent adjustments can foster a more supportive environment in the long run without creating unnecessary friction in your relationships.

Answer_with_writing_sample: Idli, the fluffy rice cake that may seem like a healthy breakfast option, does have its drawbacks! First off, while it's low in calories, idlis can be quite bland and often lack the flavor punch that maybe you crave in the morning. Plus, they’re primarily made of rice, which has a high glycemic index – great for a quick energy boost but not the best for keeping your blood sugar stable, especially if you're dipping into that sambhar too frequently! Another thing to consider: if you're not mindful of portion sizes, those seemingly innocent idlis can add up and may lead to unwanted weight gain. And let’s not forget, they are best enjoyed fresh, so if you’re eating leftover idlis, the texture turns pretty rubbery and unappealing, which can ruin your breakfast experience. So, while idlis might be a staple for many, it's wise to enjoy them in moderation and pair them with nutrient-rich sides to avoid a breakfast mishap!
Answer_with_user_profile: While idli, a popular South Indian dish made from fermented rice and lentil batter, is often praised for its nutritional profile, there are several disadvantages to consider when consuming this staple food. Firstly, idlis are relatively low in protein compared to other breakfast options, which can be a concern for those needing a higher protein intake for muscle repair or other health reasons. Additionally, the fermentation process, while beneficial for digestion, can lead to a high level of histamines in some individuals, potentially causing allergic reactions or discomfort. Those with specific food intolerances or allergies should also be cautious; for instance, the use of certain lentils or rice varieties may not suit everyone. Moreover, since idlis are typically served with accompaniments like coconut chutney and sambar, the overall meal may inadvertently become high in calories and fats, depending on how generously these sides are added. Individuals who are sensitive to carbohydrates might also find that the rice base can lead to rapid spikes in blood sugar levels. Lastly, many store-bought idlis may contain preservatives or additives, which can be detrimental to health if consumed frequently. Therefore, while idlis can be a wholesome part of a balanced diet, moderation and awareness of personal dietary needs and reactions are crucial for optimal health.
Answer_with_full_information: While idli is often lauded for its health benefits, there are a few disadvantages to consider, particularly when consumed in excess or without adequate balance in one’s diet. First, idli is primarily made of rice and urad dal, which are rich in carbohydrates and may lead to spikes in blood sugar levels, especially for those diabetic or pre-diabetic. Though idlis are low in calories, they are not particularly high in protein when compared to other options, which might not suit those looking for a protein-rich meal to maintain muscle mass or satiety. Additionally, some individuals may experience digestive issues, such as bloating or gas, because idli is fermented, which might not sit well with everyone’s digestive system. There’s also the concern of over-reliance on this staple food; consuming idli too frequently without incorporating other grains, vegetables, or proteins can result in nutritional deficiencies over time. Moreover, excessive consumption can contribute to a monotonous diet, preventing individuals from enjoying a diverse range of flavors and nutrients offered by other food varieties. Lastly, as idlis are often served with chutneys or sambar, one must be cautious about the ingredients and portion sizes of these accompaniments, as they can add significant calories, sodium, or sugars, potentially counteracting the health benefits of the idli itself. Therefore, while idli can be a beneficial component of a balanced diet, moderation and variety are key to ensuring one’s overall health and nutrition.

Answer_with_writing_sample: Intermittent fasting can be a rollercoaster ride, especially with something as intense as two 36-hour fasts a week! It’s great that you're managing to lose and sustain 1-2 pounds, but weight fluctuations happen—it’s totally normal! Sometimes, your body plays tricks on you; it might be holding onto water weight, especially after a long fast. Maybe you indulged a bit more post-fast or your body is adapting to the fasting schedule. Remember, results aren’t always linear. Are you tracking your overall caloric intake? Hydration levels? Don’t get discouraged; your body might just be recalibrating. Keep it up, and remember—progress isn’t just about the numbers on the scale!
Answer_with_user_profile: It’s not uncommon to experience fluctuations in weight during intermittent fasting, even after successful fasts. There are several factors that could explain why you didn’t lose any weight after your recent 36-hour fast. Firstly, weight loss isn’t always linear; it can be influenced by water retention, muscle gain, or hormonal changes in your body. After a prolonged fast, your body may retain more water due to factors such as glycogen replenishment or hormonal adjustments. Secondly, your body may be adapting to the fasting regimen, slowing down metabolism as it becomes more efficient at conserving energy. Additionally, the types of food you eat during your feeding windows can have a significant impact on weight loss; higher calorie intake, even on non-fasting days, can offset the calorie deficit created during fasting. Stress, sleep quality, and hydration levels also play crucial roles in weight management; insufficient sleep or high stress can lead to hormonal imbalances that affect hunger and weight. Lastly, it could simply be a temporary plateau; sometimes, giving your body time to adjust can lead to further weight loss in the following weeks. It's important to remember that consistency in the long term, rather than focusing solely on day-to-day fluctuations, is key to achieving sustainable results. If you're concerned, consider monitoring your overall progress, adjusting your diet, or consulting with a health professional for tailored advice.
Answer_with_full_information: Intermittent fasting can be an effective method for weight management, but it's essential to understand that weight loss isn't always linear. When you fast for an extended period, your body engages in a variety of metabolic processes. However, the scale might not reflect every single effort due to various factors. Firstly, hydration plays a crucial role; if you consumed more water or salty foods during your eating window, it may lead to temporary weight retention. Additionally, your body might hold onto glycogen stores post-fast, which comes with water weight. Hormonal fluctuations, specifically cortisol and insulin levels, can also have a significant impact on weight fluctuations. Perhaps stress or lack of sleep could have influenced your hormones during this period. Furthermore, muscle mass can be a factor; if you've gained muscle, it could mask fat loss on the scale. Remember, while the scale is one metric of progress, other indicators like how your clothes fit, energy levels, or body measurements are equally important. If you’re consistently doing your fasts and maintaining a balanced diet during your eating periods, don't be discouraged by the occasional plateau. Stay patient, as fluctuations are a normal part of the journey. Keep listening to your body and adjust if necessary, but don’t let one off day skew your progress. Keep tracking, stay committed, and trust the process.

Question: Why is it important for a teacher to know how learners learn?
Old_Answer: Teaching involves a Guru (Teacher) and a Shishya (Student). The role of the teacher is not only to share information but to make students be able to analyze , question and make meaningful conclusions based on the information shared. Therefore, it is of utmost importance that teacher should learn the behavior and the learning pattern of the students in-order to choose different ways how and what information is to be shared so that the students can process the information and is able to make meaningful conclusions out of it. I once had a student who had problems in memorizing the multiplication table despite years and years of efforts by his parents and previous teachers. It was a challenge but I closely observed his learning patterns and then I had to make a whole different setup and made entire multiplication table in the form of a story using various memory techniques and the student was finally able to memorize the multiplication table. Teachers are are the ones who help the learners build a strong core foundation, therefore it is very important that a teacher knows how their learners learn. Wishing you a happy life.
Answer_with_writing_sample: Understanding how learners learn is like having a key to the classroom kingdom! Imagine you've got a garden full of diverse plants (students), and if you don’t know which ones thrive in sunlight versus shade, you’ll end up with wilted blooms. Similarly, a teacher who knows their students' learning styles can tailor their approach, ensuring each learner blossoms to their fullest potential. It’s not just about delivering information; it's about engaging, inspiring, and adapting to keep those minds curious and active. So, whether it’s visual aids for the visual learners or hands-on activities for the kinesthetic ones, knowing how learners learn shapes the whole educational experience. After all, a happy, thriving garden of learners is what we all aim for! 🌱
Answer_with_user_profile: Understanding how learners learn is crucial for teachers as it directly impacts the effectiveness of their teaching methods and the overall learning experience. Each student comes with unique backgrounds, experiences, and cognitive abilities, influencing how they absorb, process, and retain information. By comprehensively grasping diverse learning styles—be it visual, auditory, kinesthetic, or a combination—teachers can tailor their instruction to meet the specific needs of each learner. This not only fosters a more engaging classroom environment but also promotes better academic performance and motivation among students. Additionally, recognizing the psychological and emotional aspects of learning helps teachers build stronger relationships with their students, creating a supportive atmosphere where they feel valued and understood. A deeper knowledge of learning processes also empowers educators to identify potential barriers to learning and address them proactively, ensuring that every student has an equitable chance to succeed. Ultimately, when teachers are attuned to how their students learn, they can employ varied instructional strategies to enhance comprehension, stimulate critical thinking, and encourage lifelong learning, thus playing a pivotal role in shaping well-rounded individuals. This alignment between teaching and learning strategies is essential for creating resilient learners who can adapt to the challenges of an ever-evolving world.
Answer_with_full_information: Understanding how learners learn is crucial for teachers as it directly influences the effectiveness of their teaching strategies and the academic growth of their students. Each learner has a unique cognitive structure, shaped by their psychological and emotional backgrounds, experiences, and individual learning styles. By recognizing these diverse learning modalities, teachers can tailor their instruction to meet students' specific needs, fostering a more engaging and supportive learning environment. For instance, some students may thrive in collaborative settings, while others might excel through solitary study or practical application. A teacher attuned to these distinctions can implement differentiated instruction, ensuring that every student not only understands the material but also feels empowered in their learning journey. Moreover, when educators grasp how learners absorb and process information, they can better anticipate challenges and misconceptions, addressing them proactively and transforming potential roadblocks into opportunities for deeper understanding. This, in turn, builds student confidence and encourages a growth mindset. Ultimately, acknowledging and embracing the varied ways in which learners engage with content allows for a more personalized and impactful educational experience, leading to higher motivation, deeper comprehension, and long-term academic success. In a rapidly changing world, a teacher’s knowledge of learner variability is not just beneficial—it is essential for cultivating curious, critical thinkers ready to tackle future challenges.
